bounded_recoveries.description: The exact original process was inspected and allowed to finish without replay; it produced and staged the 519-entry evidence manifest plus two declared self-exclusions.
A separate read-only process and Git-index audit showed CPU progress, retained the same process identity, and confirmed the staged index remained intact.
The CPU scalar was materialized before comparison; the same original process remained attributable and then completed without replay.
A compact read-only Git audit recovered the exact evidence commit, parent, two-commit lifecycle count, clean state, 0/0 divergence, and fresh four-way equality.
The recovery recognized previously adjudicated staged-review records as scanner metadata while preserving all five class scans; zero confirmed payload hits remained.

The manifest-parity test transport was changed from per-entry Git process spawning to one index/tree map and one streaming batch reader; the separately identified corrected precommit selection then completed with an attributable result.

failed_witnesses.description: The first evidence-manifest wrapper crossed its bounded projection window without an attributable result while the original Python process remained active.
The first bounded Wait-Process audit returned no attributable projection while the original manifest process was still active.
A later wait-and-status projection used an inline PowerShell conditional where a scalar value was required and failed after the wait.
The evidence-commit tool projection truncated the large create-file listing before presenting an attributable compact completion summary.
The first final-manifest preflight classified two inherited staged-review scanner-class labels as payload hits solely because those adjudication records were JSON rather than Python.

The first final precommit test wrapper crossed its projection window after four progress markers; the original process later ended after its output handle was lost, leaving no attributable exit code or test summary.
